name: DAR reconciliation - method
was: README reported the 1948-50 DAR survey as turning up many stones the modern sources missed (about 54 unmatched over 16 pages)
now: FALSE on both counts. (a) reconcile_dar.py matched on surname-soundex + ANY year overlap with no one-to-one constraint, so it both over-matched (it paired 'Unmarked grave in Cox lot' with a real burial) and, once tightened, threw up spurious non-matches; (b) the first-pass transcription had systematic reading errors. After a second pass at high zoom and a strict matcher: 443 entries, 407 exact matches (92%), 12 date conflicts, 14 undated, 10 unmatched - of which only 3 look like real gaps.
note: Specific first-pass misreadings: Mock->'Hock' (10 entries), Wine->'Vine' (3), Moatz->'Hoats' (2), Fincham->'Pincham' (3), Mossburg->'Vossburg' (2), Seaton->'Gaston', Verts->'Yerts', Sagrario->'Saggario', plus a recurring 2/3 digit confusion in years (1888->1889, 1928->1938, 1823->1853, 1920->1930, 1902->1908, 1927->1937, 1898->1892, 1867->1897). Use transcripts/dar1948_lakeview_VERIFIED.txt and reconcile_dar2.py; the first-pass files are marked superseded.

name: George Franklin Everhart
was: 1828-vs-1842 birth conflict unresolved; no parents identified
now: LV0395 William N. Everhart (Oct 23, 1817 - Jan 10, 1903) and LV0396 Catharine S. Everhart (Sept 5, 1820 - Dec 5, 1862) are almost certainly his parents, which makes the stone's 1828 impossible and favours 1842
note: DAR entries 423-425 (page 16) give the parents and a daughter Annie A. b. Feb 20, 1844. The 1860 Southern District household (ark M41J-FJ1) is 'William W Everheart 42, Catherine 44, Mary S 19, George F 18, Arrabella 15, Lydia J 13, William W 8'. Two children tie that household to Lakeview stones exactly: 'Arrabella 15' = LV0397 Annie Arabella Everhart b. Feb 20, 1844 (age 16 in June 1860), and 'Lydia J 13' = LV0285 Lydia Jane Everhart Cummings b. July 5, 1846 (DAR entry 427), age 13 - an exact match. William N. b. Oct 1817 is 42 in June 1860, matching the head of household exactly. So the household is William N. Everhart's, and the 'George F 18' in it was born c.1842. A man born 1817 cannot have fathered a son in 1828. ASSUMPTION, stated plainly: that the George F. Everhart buried at Lakeview (d. June 25, 1918) is the son in that household. Supporting it: his parents, his sister Annie Arabella and his sister Lydia Jane are all buried at Lakeview, and he lies there with his wife. CAVEAT: the census gives Catherine's age as 44, which would put her birth c.1816, not 1820 - a five-year discrepancy. And both Balch and the 1948-50 DAR survey read the stone as Jan. 12, 1828 (entry 295, re-verified at high zoom today), so if 1842 is right the error is in the stone itself or in its cutting, not in the two readings of it.
